prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create a flat production UV texture atlas for the inside of fictional aircraft and tracked exploration vehicles in a video game. Exactly four square tiles in an exact edge-to-edge 2x2 grid. All textures completely front-on, orthographic, no perspective, no scene, no vehicle exterior, no people, no outer border and no gutters. TOP LEFT: sophisticated aviation multifunction flight display on dark navy glass, fine cyan and mint technical lines, blue/brown artificial horizon with pitch ladder, navigation map inset, fine altitude and airspeed numerals, restrained realistic screen illumination without bloom. TOP RIGHT: green phosphor engineering navigation display on nearly black glass, fine circular compass, digital range and bearing scales, thin terrain contour grid, small status readouts and subtle CRT sensor grain, no objects or weapons. BOTTOM LEFT: only a seamless neutral charcoal anodized metal surface texture, subtle brushed micrograin, small faded abrasion and hairline scratches, evenly lit, no objects or lettering. BOTTOM RIGHT: black analog aviation instrument panel faceplate, four detailed circular dial faces in a 2x2 layout, fine ivory ticks and numerals, small amber needles, tasteful cyan accents. Crisp restrained realistic instrument art, designed to be mapped onto 3D geometry. No logos, no watermark, no baked perspective shadows.
usage: Blender UV atlas for shared cockpit screens and worn metal; live avionics are drawn over the display tiles.
